raw_response:
I've been farming this land in Quzhou for twenty years. I know what works here. My husband and oldest son do some outside work in the slow season, so I can't depend on them fully during peak labor times — I need to plan around that.

My 10.1 mu breaks down like this in my head: I'll keep the wheat-maize rotation on 7 mu because that's stable income and I know exactly what to do. I'll put 3.1 mu in cotton. Cotton prices have been okay and I have the irrigation from the well to manage it, but I won't expand it because the picking is exhausting when it's just me and my mother-in-law.

For wheat this winter, I'll use Kenong 199 — my neighbor switched to it three years ago and hasn't looked back. I apply base fertilizer before seeding, then topdress at jointing. Three irrigations: once before sowing to get the seedbed right, once at jointing, once at heading. I've done this for years.

For summer maize, I go straight into no-till after wheat harvest — saves time when I'm rushing. Zhengdan 958 hybrid. The well handles two irrigations: at tasseling if it's dry, and at grain fill.

For cotton, I use the Bt hybrid seed — cuts down on bollworm spraying a lot. Still need to watch for aphids and spider mites, so I keep about four pesticide applications in mind. Cotton needs more potassium on my soil. Four irrigations to keep it through the dry spells.
